rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for rna_only models. This tests the simplest configuration (singleprofile, PCA encoder) to provide a reference point for comparing more complex setups later. It clarifies the baseline performance of RNA-only models, which is critical for understanding if multimodal approaches offer meaningful improvements.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration (testing multiprofile) and exploitation (using the same RNA encoder as config_001) to determine if these changes improve accuracy without altering too many factors at once.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile variants. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (while keeping multiprofile and avgpool aggregation) improves accuracy, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder choice. This balances exploration of key design choices with building on the promising multiprofile setting.

Existing evidence shows that config_005 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.650124). This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method from avgpool to transformer (config_006) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation. It builds on the promising direction of scvi_n200 with multiprofile while exploring a key design choice (aggregation) that could further enhance accuracy.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.653). This experiment tests combining this strong RNA encoder with a powerful image encoder (resnet50) and transformer aggregation, using concat fusion to isolate the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploitation of current best components with exploration of multimodal potential, which could yield higher accuracy if image data adds value.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l encoders achieve the highest accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted in config_038 improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best use of the remaining budget to further optimize the top-performing multimodal configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt (a more advanced RNA encoder) in the same multimodal setup improves accuracy, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder. This is a focused exploration of a key design choice with potential to either confirm or challenge the current leading configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with scvi_n200, ViT, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether using scgpt (a different RNA encoder) with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (same as config_039) can match or exceed performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder. This is the best use of the remaining budget to evaluate a critical design choice (RNA encoder) while maintaining the successful aggregation and fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder, using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests a similar setup but with scgpt RNA encoder and concat fusion, which could clarify whether RNA encoder choice or fusion method has a greater impact. It is the best use of the final experiment to explore a critical design choice (RNA encoder vs. fusion method) that may influence performance.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy of 0.724989. This experiment tests a similar configuration but with pca_n2000 RNA encoder, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. Since this is the final experiment, testing this configuration clarifies whether the RNA encoder is the key factor or if other variations could slightly improve performance.
